kakadu-national-park-1.name: Ubirr
kakadu-national-park-1.bio: Rock art galleries on a short walk, then a climb to a sunset lookout over the floodplains.
kakadu-national-park-1.hours: Open daily in the Dry; access limited in the Wet
kakadu-national-park-1.coordinates_source: OSM highway=footway 'Ubirr Aboriginal Art Walk' (photon); Wikipedia -12.4095,132.9593 and Commons median within 300 m
kakadu-national-park-1.notes: Cost is the Kakadu park pass (AUD 25 Wet/discount to 31 Oct 2026, 40 Dry); no separate fee. Hours unsourced.

kakadu-national-park-2.name: Nourlangie Rock
kakadu-national-park-2.bio: Rock art shelter under the escarpment, reached by an easy walk to the main gallery and a lookout.
kakadu-national-park-2.coordinates_source: OSM historic=archaeological_site 'Burrungkuy (Nourlangie Rock)' (photon); Wikipedia -12.8617,132.8125 within 250 m. MEDIUM
kakadu-national-park-2.notes: resolve-pin printed LOW (single OSM feature, but the exact site of the right type).

kakadu-national-park-3.name: Yellow Water
kakadu-national-park-3.bio: Billabong on the floodplain, cruised by boat from Cooinda for birds and crocodiles.
kakadu-national-park-3.coordinates_source: OSM amenity=ferry_terminal 'Yellow Water Cruises' (photon); Commons median 750 m
kakadu-national-park-3.notes: Cruise price approximate (1.5 h about 105, 2 h sunrise/sunset about 130, operator rates 2025 via search/Expedia); park pass extra. Pin is the cruise terminal (visitor point), not the billabong centroid.

kakadu-national-park-4.name: Jim Jim Falls
kakadu-national-park-4.bio: Tallest waterfall in the park, at the end of a 4WD track and a rock-hopping walk to a plunge pool.
kakadu-national-park-4.coordinates_source: OSM waterway=waterfall 'Jim Jim Falls' (photon); Wikipedia 42 m
kakadu-national-park-4.notes: CLOSED all of 2026 (road works; target reopening 2027 Dry season). Owner call on adding now.

kakadu-national-park-5.name: Twin Falls
kakadu-national-park-5.bio: Waterfall in the Arnhem Land escarpment, reached by a 4WD track and a walk to the gorge base.
kakadu-national-park-5.coordinates_source: OSM place=locality 'Twin Falls' (photon); Commons median 78 m; Wikipedia 347 m
kakadu-national-park-5.notes: Gorge closed since 2019 and all of 2026; reopening tied to boardwalk project. Bio drops the old boat-shuttle claim (not stated on the agency page). Recommend HOLD.

kakadu-national-park-6.name: Gunlom
kakadu-national-park-6.bio: Waterfall and clifftop plunge pools above a steep climb in the south of the park, with wide views.
kakadu-national-park-6.coordinates_source: OSM waterway=waterfall 'Gunlom Waterfall' (photon); Commons median 14 m
kakadu-national-park-6.notes: Agency page: no swimming in the bottom pool. Dry-season-only from Wikivoyage; hours unsourced.

kakadu-national-park-7.name: Maguk
kakadu-national-park-7.bio: Plunge pool below a waterfall in monsoon rainforest, reached by a short walk from a 4WD track.
kakadu-national-park-7.coordinates_source: OSM waterway=waterfall 'Maguk Waterfall' (photon); Wikipedia 4 m of earlier hint
kakadu-national-park-7.notes: Agency page shows a temporary crocodile closure; walk 2 km return, 1.5 h.

kakadu-national-park-8.name: Bowali Visitor Centre
kakadu-national-park-8.bio: Visitor centre in Jabiru with displays on the park's ecology and Aboriginal culture, a gallery and a film.
kakadu-national-park-8.coordinates_source: OSM information=office 'Bowali Visitor's Centre' (photon); Wikivoyage -12.67548 within 55 m. MEDIUM
kakadu-national-park-8.notes: Printed LOW by resolve-pin (one precise OSM feature). Closed Christmas Day and New Year's Day. Free entry per Wikivoyage; agency page names no fee.

kakadu-national-park-9.name: Warradjan Aboriginal Cultural Centre
kakadu-national-park-9.bio: Cultural centre at Yellow Water with exhibits on the traditional owners' story of the park and local art.
kakadu-national-park-9.coordinates_source: OSM building 'Warradjan Aboriginal Cultural Centre' (photon); Wikivoyage -12.8986,132.5267 within 50 m. MEDIUM
kakadu-national-park-9.notes: Entry fee not stated on agency page; free assumed (unverified).

kakadu-national-park-10.name: Mamukala Wetlands
kakadu-national-park-10.bio: Wetlands with a bird hide on an easy 3 km return walk, filling with magpie geese by late August.
kakadu-national-park-10.coordinates_source: OSM leisure=bird_hide 'Mamukala Wetlands Observation Deck' node 282618975 (Overpass); viewing platform node 4835919424 and 'Mamukala Wetlands Walk' within 100 m. MEDIUM
kakadu-national-park-10.notes: resolve-pin LOW (no result); pin from Overpass. Hours unsourced.

kakadu-national-park-11.name: Cahills Crossing
kakadu-national-park-11.bio: Tidal causeway on the East Alligator River, a viewing platform for watching estuarine crocodiles.
kakadu-national-park-11.hours: Open daily; time visits to the tide
kakadu-national-park-11.coordinates_source: OSM way 178561642 bridge=low_water_crossing (Overpass center) agrees with Commons median -12.4269,132.9653 (3 m). MEDIUM. Placement's Wikipedia point is 60 km west and wrong
kakadu-national-park-11.notes: Best July to November. Never cross on foot.

kakadu-national-park-12.name: Anbangbang Billabong
kakadu-national-park-12.bio: Billabong on a 2.5 km loop walk near Nourlangie, with birds and a view back to the rock.
kakadu-national-park-12.coordinates_source: OSM highway=footway 'Anbangbang Billabong Walk' (photon) with natural=wetland 22 m and Wikipedia 8 m. HIGH
kakadu-national-park-12.notes: Loop may open in stages in the Dry by water level. Pinned at the billabong shore on the loop, not the loop midpoint.

destination.name: Kakadu National Park
destination.tagline: Floodplains, escarpment waterfalls and Aboriginal rock art across a World Heritage park east of Darwin.
destination.description: Kakadu National Park covers about 20,000 square kilometres of floodplain, woodland and sandstone escarpment, and is World Heritage listed for both its nature and its culture. Rock art galleries at Ubirr and Nourlangie sit beside billabongs thick with birds and saltwater crocodiles. In the south, Gunlom and Maguk have waterfalls and plunge pools reached on dirt roads. Bowali Visitor Centre at Jabiru is the place to start.
whyVisit: See rock art at Ubirr and Nourlangie
Cruise Yellow Water for crocodiles and birds
Climb to Gunlom's clifftop plunge pools

goodToKnow.title: Park pass required
goodToKnow.detail: A Kakadu park pass lasts seven days: adults $40 in the Dry ($25 until 31 Oct 2026), $25 in the Wet. NT residents are free.

goodToKnow.title: Check the access report
goodToKnow.detail: Floods, fires and crocodile sightings close roads and sites, and Maguk needs a 4WD. Check the Kakadu Access Report before driving.

goodToKnow.title: Be crocwise
goodToKnow.detail: Saltwater crocodiles live in these waterways. Swim only where signs allow, and never cross Cahills Crossing on foot.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: The Dry season, {months}, opens the roads and walks and fills the billabongs with birds; in the Wet many falls and tracks are cut off.
